place.rowan_grove.name: the rowan wood
quest.waxwing.title: A waxwing for Sorokin
quest.waxwing.desc: A retired ornithologist lives in the Academgorodok. They say he knows everything about the birds here.
quest.waxwing.find.log: Sorokin is the one to ask about birds. He is a retired ornithologist and lives in the Academgorodok. He gets up before dawn, and by day he sits with his binoculars on a bench in the square: from eight to half past twelve and from half past two to half past six.
quest.waxwing.talk_sorokin.obj: Find Sorokin the ornithologist and talk to him
quest.waxwing.prepare.log: Sorokin said: the guide first, then the feed. The guide is in the Academgorodok's library; the grocery sells dried rowan and a feeder. He studied waxwings for forty years and has not seen one here: they keep to the old forest beyond the northern hills, and he can't walk that far any more. I'll go.
quest.waxwing.get_guide.obj: Take the bird guide from the library
quest.waxwing.get_rowan.obj: Buy dried rowan at the grocery
quest.waxwing.get_feeder.obj: Buy a bird feeder at the grocery
quest.waxwing.journey.log: I have everything. The waxwings live far to the north: across the whole town and on, in the old forest on the hills, where the rowans are. It is a long walk.
quest.waxwing.reach_grove.obj: Walk to the old forest beyond the northern hills
quest.waxwing.lure.log: This is the forest. There are rowans at every step. I should put the feeder up on level open ground and pour dried rowan into it.
quest.waxwing.fill_feeder.obj: Put the feeder up in the forest and fill it with rowan
quest.waxwing.wait.log: The feeder is up. Sorokin said birds find the feed in an hour and a half or two, and only by day: towards evening they are already off to roost. Step back twenty paces, crouch and keep still.
quest.waxwing.see_waxwing.obj: Wait by the feeder until a waxwing comes
quest.waxwing.tame.log: They have come. A crest, a yellow band on the tail, red drops on the wings. Now creep up quite slowly, crouching, and hold out a palm with rowan. No hurry.
quest.waxwing.tame_waxwing.obj: Feed a waxwing from the palm
quest.waxwing.return.log: I am a waxwing. Sorokin wanted to see just one. By day he sits on a bench in the Academgorodok's square; at night he sleeps. Find him, come down beside him and call. If I lose the waxwing's shape: back to the rowan wood and feed one from the palm again.
quest.waxwing.call_sorokin.obj: As the waxwing, find Sorokin, land beside him and call (F)
quest.waxwing.done: He knew me. Not me, of course. The waxwing. Forty years he went after them, and this one came by itself.
quest.waxwing_after.title: What Sorokin saw
quest.waxwing_after.desc: A waxwing came to Sorokin. I wonder what he will say about it.
quest.waxwing_after.visit.log: I should drop in on Sorokin as a person now. And say nothing.
quest.waxwing_after.done: Sorokin entered the waxwing in his field journal and gave me feed from his own stock. Not a word about me in the journal. As it should be.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_meet.1: You're here about birds? Then you've come to the right man. Sorokin, ornithologist. Retired, but the birds don't know that.
line.hero.waxwing_meet.2: They eat from the hand here. Is that normal?
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_meet.3: It happens, if you don't hurry. But first learn to tell them apart. My guide is in the library; ask Olya.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_meet.4: And buy proper feed. The grocery has everything, from grain to dried rowan. The sunflower seeds from the vending machine are only good for pigeons.
line.hero.waxwing_meet.5: And which birds did you study?
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_meet.6: Waxwings. Forty years. A crest, red drops on the wings, a voice like a little silver bell.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_meet.7: And here I haven't seen a single one. They keep to the old forest beyond the northern hills, where the rowans are. I can't walk that far any more: my knees.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_meet.9: An hour's walk north, across the whole town and beyond. Without rowan and a feeder a waxwing won't come near you. It is a careful bird.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_tips.1: The guide is in the library, the rowan and the feeder at the grocery, the waxwings in the north beyond the hills. Don't mix them up.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_wait.1: Put the feeder in the open, but near trees. Fill it, step back, crouch. And wait. A bird tests a person with time.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_back.1: You look like someone who is up to something. Don't tell me. I only like surprises from birds.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_seen.2: A waxwing. Here. It came by itself.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_seen.3: Forty years I went after you. Well, hello.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_again.1: You again. Sit closer, I don't bite.
line.sorokin_oleg.bird_over.1: Who is that calling? Come down, show yourself. I haven't got my binoculars.
line.sorokin_oleg.bird_visit.1: Hello, hello. Not a waxwing, but good all the same.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_after.1: A waxwing came to me. It sat down beside me and called. To me, straight to me.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_after.3: Forty years I went after them, and this one came by itself. That isn't luck, young man. That is courtesy.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_after.4: Take these. Mealworms and peanuts, from my own stock. You need them more than I do.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_journal.1: I entered it in the journal. Waxwing, one, adult. Under “behaviour” I wrote: said hello.
line.girl_b.waxwing_guide.1: The bird guide? Sorokin sent you, didn't he? There it is, on my desk.
line.girl_b.waxwing_guide.2: Just take it. He wrote it himself and told me to give it to anyone who asks about birds.
line.orlova_tanya.waxwing_rowan.1: Dried rowan? Only Sorokin ever bought it. He kept waiting for his waxwings.
line.orlova_tanya.waxwing_rowan.2: There's a feeder too. Without one the thrushes will carry your rowan off before you can blink.
quest.evening_paper.title: A paper for Nina
quest.evening_paper.desc: Nina Korneeva knows the whole yard. What she hasn't got is the evening paper.
quest.evening_paper.ask.log: Nina Korneeva lives in the Academgorodok's yard. She is worth knowing: she knows everybody here.
quest.evening_paper.buy.log: Nina asked for the evening paper. They sell it at the news stall on the fair square, in the lower town by the sea, but the stall is open only at weekends. The same paper is in the press machine in the cable car lobby. It is far for her and on my way.
quest.evening_paper.get_paper.obj: Buy the evening paper: on the fair square or from the machine at the station
quest.evening_paper.bring.log: I have the paper. It smells of printer's ink. Take it to Nina while it is fresh.
quest.evening_paper.give_paper.obj: Take the paper to Nina Korneeva
quest.evening_paper.done: Nina got her paper, and I got two pies and all the news of the yard. It seems they know me here now.
line.korneeva_nina.paper_ask.1: New here? I know everybody. I don't know you yet, but that won't last.
line.korneeva_nina.paper_ask.2: Since you walk back and forth anyway, bring me the evening paper. From the news stall on the fair square.
line.korneeva_nina.paper_ask.3: The sea is a long way for me. And without the chess problem my Vanya is unbearable of an evening.
line.korneeva_nina.paper_wait.1: You haven't forgotten the paper? The fair square is in the lower town, by the sea. You can't miss it, it's noisy.
line.korneeva_nina.paper_thanks.1: Now that's kind. Fresh, smells of ink. Keep the change.
line.korneeva_nina.paper_thanks.2: And take some pies, I baked them myself. Cabbage. So thin, it hurts to look at you.
line.korneeva_nina.paper_thanks.3: And if it's birds you like, go to Sorokin. He can talk about them till night. I've checked.
quest.crow_gift.title: The crow's button
quest.crow_gift.desc: A crow carried off Yuki's button. They say crows can do more than steal.
quest.crow_gift.ask.log: In the Academgorodok's yard a girl, Yuki Sato, is looking for something under the trees and glaring at the crows.
quest.crow_gift.feed.log: A crow carried off Yuki's shiny button. Her father says that if you feed crows they remember you and bring presents. Take feed in the hand and throw them a handful. More than once.
quest.crow_gift.gift.log: The crows have noticed me. One of them no longer looks at me like a stranger. Keep feeding them and wait: if one brings something and leaves it near me, pick it up.
quest.crow_gift.take_gift.obj: Wait for a crow's present and pick it up
quest.crow_gift.tell.log: A crow brought a present and laid it on the ground two steps away. Not a button. But Yuki should see it all the same. After school, from four, she sits on a bench in the square.
quest.crow_gift.done: The crow never gave the button back. But Yuki is not afraid of them any more, and now there is a crow I know.
line.sato_yuki.crow_ask.1: A crow stole my button. A shiny one, off my coat. Right off the bench.
line.sato_yuki.crow_ask.3: Papa says crows are clever. If you feed them they bring presents. Maybe they'll bring the button too.
line.sato_yuki.crow_ask.4: Only I'm scared of them. They look at me as if they knew everything about me. You feed them.
line.sato_yuki.crow_wait.1: Well, did it bring it? No? Keep feeding them. Papa never lies. Almost.
line.sato_yuki.crow_tell.1: It brought something?! Show me! Oh. That's not a button.
line.hero.crow_tell.2: But it brought it by itself. And laid it down beside me.
line.sato_yuki.crow_tell.3: Then she isn't a thief. She swaps. You keep it, and tomorrow I'll leave her something myself. Here, have some sweets.
quest.fisherman_cheese.title: Cheese for the fisherman
quest.fisherman_cheese.desc: Pyotr Lange has eaten nothing but fish for twenty years. He wants cheese.
quest.fisherman_cheese.ask.log: Pyotr Lange, the fisherman, says little. But I think he needs something.
quest.fisherman_cheese.buy.log: Lange asked for a cheese braid. Aslan sells them at the tent by the club. The fisherman never goes up there himself: you don't leave a boat, he says.
quest.fisherman_cheese.get_cheese.obj: Buy a cheese braid from Aslan by the club
quest.fisherman_cheese.bring.log: I have the braid. Salty, smells of smoke. Take it to Lange before I eat it myself. In the afternoon he mends nets on a bench on the promenade.
quest.fisherman_cheese.give_cheese.obj: Take the cheese to Pyotr Lange
quest.fisherman_cheese.done: Lange got his cheese, and I got worms and a herring. I think he considers it a fair trade.
line.lange_pyotr.cheese_ask.1: Twenty years of fish. Fish in the morning, fish at night. Fish in my dreams too.
line.lange_pyotr.cheese_ask.2: There's a Circassian selling cheese by the club. Smoked braids. Bring me one. I won't forget it.
line.lange_pyotr.cheese_wait.1: Cheese. A braid. By the club. That's all I have to say.
line.lange_pyotr.cheese_thanks.1: That's the one. Smells of smoke. Good.
line.lange_pyotr.cheese_thanks.2: Here, worms. And a herring, this morning's. Get yourself a rod and come by, I'll show you where they bite.
quest.window_feeder.title: The window bet
quest.window_feeder.desc: Dasha and Vika have a bet on whether anything but pigeons lives in the yard. Only an experiment can settle it.
quest.window_feeder.ask.log: Dasha Kimura, the student, is arguing with her flatmate and looking at me as if I were a piece of equipment.
quest.window_feeder.fill.log: Dasha has a bet with Vika, who says the yard has nothing but pigeons. An experiment is needed. Put up a feeder in the Academgorodok and fill it. The grocery has feeders and feed.
quest.window_feeder.fill_feeder.obj: Put up a feeder and fill it
quest.window_feeder.watch.log: The feeder is full. Now step back, sit down and count who comes. Science takes patience. And keeping still.
quest.window_feeder.count_birds.obj: Wait for visitors at the feeder
quest.window_feeder.tell.log: Five visits, and not a single pigeon. Dasha will like it. Vika won't. Dasha is easiest to find in the square after five.
quest.window_feeder.done: Dasha won the bet, Vika does the dishes for a week. The feeder stays in the yard. The birds don't care who was right.
line.kimura_dasha.feeder_ask.1: Wait. You're the one with the binoculars, right? Settle something for us.
line.kimura_dasha.feeder_ask.2: Vika says our yard has nothing but pigeons. I say the sample is too small. A week of dishes is riding on it.
line.hero.feeder_ask.3: We could put up a feeder and count.
line.kimura_dasha.feeder_ask.4: An experiment! Something scientific in this yard at last. Go on. I'll even accept the report orally.
line.kimura_dasha.feeder_wait.1: Well, any data? No data, no conclusion. Go and count.
line.hero.feeder_tell.2: Not one. I think the pigeons took offence.
line.kimura_dasha.feeder_tell.3: Vika! A week of dishes! And biscuits and coffee for you. It's not a bribe, it's a grant.
quest.magpie_key.title: The magpie inquiry
quest.magpie_key.desc: Misha Belov has lost a key. The suspect sits on the ledge and denies nothing.
quest.magpie_key.ask.log: In the Academgorodok Misha Belov, the Laboratory's technician, walks about looking not at his feet but at the roofs. At the magpies, to be exact.
quest.magpie_key.search.log: Misha has lost the key to his toolbox. He is sure a magpie took it. He asked me to pick up three of the things magpies and crows carry about: off the ground (E), or out of a store if I saw the bird bury it. A cone or a nut will do as evidence too.
quest.magpie_key.gather_finds.obj: Pick up the magpies' and crows' finds
quest.magpie_key.tell.log: Three finds. Not one of them looks like a toolbox key. Show them to Misha: on weekdays he is out after half past four, at weekends all day.
quest.magpie_key.tell_misha.obj: Show the finds to Misha Belov
quest.magpie_key.done: All that time the key was hanging on a magnet on Misha's workbench. The magpie is cleared and got half a biscuit. I got a chocolate bar, and the finds stayed with me.
line.belov_misha.magpie_ask.1: You haven't seen a magpie with a key in its bill, have you? A small one, from a toolbox.
line.hero.magpie_ask.2: I've seen the magpie. Not the key.
line.belov_misha.magpie_ask.3: It lay on the windowsill, shining. I turned away for a minute and it was gone. And there she sat on the ledge, looking pleased with herself.
line.belov_misha.magpie_ask.4: They carry everything off and hide it. Pick up what they leave lying about and what they bury. Once you have three things, bring them and I'll take a look.
line.belov_misha.magpie_wait.1: Well, how are the magpies? Watch where they hide things and pick them up. Three finds will do for me.
line.belov_misha.magpie_tell.1: Well then, let's see the evidence.
line.hero.magpie_tell.2: Here. Everything I managed to find of theirs.
line.belov_misha.magpie_tell.3: They live well. But my key isn't here. And to be honest, it couldn't be.
line.belov_misha.magpie_tell.4: I found it this morning. Stuck to a magnet on my workbench, right under my nose.
line.belov_misha.magpie_tell.6: Innocent. I've already apologised to her, with half a biscuit. Keep the finds, and this is for the investigation.
quest.painter_views.title: Three views of the town
quest.painter_views.desc: Aya Nishimura paints the island every day. What the town looks like from outside, she knows only from other people's stories.
quest.painter_views.ask.log: A painter lives in the Academgorodok, Aya Nishimura. She walks in the yard in the morning, then takes the train to the island. She looks at everything as if she were already painting it. Towards evening she sits with a sketchbook on a bench in the square.
quest.painter_views.look.log: Aya asked me to look at the town for her. Three places, in any order: the promenade, the starlings over the sea, and the rowan wood beyond the northern hills. The starlings are best towards evening. No drawing needed, only remembering.
quest.painter_views.see_promenade.obj: Look at the town from the promenade
quest.painter_views.see_starlings.obj: Look from where the starlings fly over the sea
quest.painter_views.tell.log: Three places, three different towns. Or one town that will not hold still. Tell Aya before I forget what colour the sky was. Towards evening she sits with a sketchbook on a bench in the square.
quest.painter_views.done: Aya listened and gave me a postcard of the island. She says she now has three paintings she never painted. The legs, for the record, were mine.
line.nishimura_aya.views_ask.1: Every day I go off to paint the island. And I have never once seen my own town from the outside.
line.nishimura_aya.views_ask.2: They say there are three places to look from. The promenade, the spot where the starlings fly over the sea at dusk, and the rowan wood beyond the northern hills.
line.nishimura_aya.views_ask.4: The morning train does not wait, and the light waits even less. Go for me. No paints needed, just look and remember.
line.nishimura_aya.views_wait.1: The promenade, the starlings, the rowan wood. Take your time. Look too fast and all you get is a postcard.
line.nishimura_aya.views_tell.1: I can see by your face that you went. Tell me. Only not in guidebook words.
line.hero.views_tell.2: From the promenade it is big and loud, and from the starlings you cannot see it for the birds. From the wood it is small and quiet.
line.nishimura_aya.views_tell.3: Small and quiet. I would never have guessed. From the inside it is nothing like that.
line.nishimura_aya.views_tell.4: Three paintings, and not one of them mine. It stings. And it is very good.
line.nishimura_aya.views_tell.5: Take a postcard, and a little for the road. It is the island, of course. But now you know what is missing from it.
quest.first_catch.title: First catch
quest.first_catch.desc: Pyotr Lange promised to show where they bite. All it takes is a rod.
quest.first_catch.rod.log: Lange said: get a rod and he will show me where they bite. Tanya Orlova sells rods at the grocery in the Academgorodok. The plainest one is ninety rubles.
quest.first_catch.get_rod.obj: Buy a fishing rod at the grocery
quest.first_catch.learn.log: I have a rod. It folds up and smells of the shop, not of the sea. Now to find Lange. He is out at sea until eleven in the morning; after that he can be found ashore.
quest.first_catch.hear_spot.obj: Show the rod to Pyotr Lange
quest.first_catch.catch.log: Lange said: the end of the pier, a worm on the hook, and no striking too soon. It sounds simple. We shall see what the fish think of it.
quest.first_catch.catch_fish.obj: Catch a fish from the pier
quest.first_catch.tell.log: Caught one. Myself, on my own rod. The fish regards me without enthusiasm. I should tell Lange. In the afternoon he mends nets on a bench on the promenade.
quest.first_catch.tell_lange.obj: Tell Pyotr Lange about the catch
quest.first_catch.done: Lange gave me his old spoon lure and said more words in a row than in all the time I have known him. He has remembered his first goby for forty years. I expect I will remember my fish too.
line.lange_pyotr.catch_norod.1: I see no rod. Tanya has them at the grocery, ninety rubles. Without one there's nothing to show.
line.lange_pyotr.catch_learn.1: So you bought one. Telescopic. It'll do to start with.
line.lange_pyotr.catch_learn.2: Go out on the pier, right to the end. It's deep there, the fish hold by the piles.
line.hero.catch_learn.3: What do I use for bait?
line.lange_pyotr.catch_learn.4: A worm. When the float twitches, leave it. When it goes under, then you strike.
line.lange_pyotr.catch_learn.5: And don't pull while she's pulling. A line is not a rope. Catch one and come back.
line.lange_pyotr.catch_wait.1: The pier, a worm and patience. The fish will come by themselves. Just see that you're there, not here.
line.lange_pyotr.catch_tell.2: I can tell by your face. The first is always the biggest, whatever it weighs.
line.lange_pyotr.catch_tell.3: I've remembered my first for forty years. A goby, the size of my palm. My father laughed.
line.lange_pyotr.catch_tell.4: Take this spoon. Old, but it catches. From here on you'll work out for yourself where they bite.
quest.sparrow_hello.title: A sparrow says hello
quest.sparrow_hello.desc: Sonya has tested it: birds do not make friends with people. She tested it once, on one sparrow.
quest.sparrow_hello.ask.log: Sonya from the club, the one at the iMac, is looking at me as if she has an important conclusion ready.
quest.sparrow_hello.tame.log: Sonya said hello to a sparrow and it flew away. Now she is sure birds do not make friends with people. She will believe it only if a sparrow comes and says hello first. The vending machine in the club sells feed. House sparrows keep to the houses and the club door. Crouch, hold out a palm, keep still.
quest.sparrow_hello.tame_sparrow.obj: Feed a house sparrow from the palm
quest.sparrow_hello.call.log: I am a sparrow. The world got bigger and the crumbs easier to see. Find Sonya, sit close and chirp. If she is in the club, I will have to hop in to her from the door. In the morning she is at school, after nine in the evening she is asleep.
quest.sparrow_hello.call_sonya.obj: As the sparrow, sit near Sonya and call (F)
quest.sparrow_hello.tell.log: She said hello back. I think she even introduced herself. Now to come back as a person and hear what she makes of it.
quest.sparrow_hello.tell_sonya.obj: Come back as yourself and talk to Sonya
quest.sparrow_hello.done: Sonya now says hello to every sparrow she meets. Some of them answer, she says. I do not argue.
line.kid_girl.sparrow_ask.1: Birds don't make friends with people. I tested it.
line.kid_girl.sparrow_ask.3: I said hello to a sparrow. It flew away. Didn't even think about it.
line.kid_girl.sparrow_ask.4: Now, if a sparrow came over and said hello first, then I'd believe it.
line.kid_girl.sparrow_wait.1: No sparrow has come yet. I'm keeping watch.
line.kid_girl.sparrow_seen.2: Is that for me? Did you really come all by yourself?
line.kid_girl.sparrow_seen.3: Hello. I'm Sonya. Just don't fly away right off, okay?
line.kid_girl.sparrow_other.1: You're a pretty bird. But the deal was about a sparrow.
line.kid_girl.sparrow_tell.1: A sparrow came to see me. By itself. It sat down and said cheep.
line.kid_girl.sparrow_tell.3: Hello. And it didn't fly away. So they do make friends. I was wrong, but only a tiny bit.
line.kid_girl.sparrow_tell.4: Here, have a chocolate bar. Mum left me two, for the hour. The hour ran out long ago.
quest.soda_science.title: A blind tasting
quest.soda_science.desc: Galina Zotova, a chemist, suspects the four sodas in the club's vending machine are really one. She needs a taster with no degree.
quest.soda_science.ask.log: Galina Zotova lives in the Academgorodok, a chemist from the Laboratory. She looks at me as if choosing my sample number.
quest.soda_science.taste.log: Galina thinks the club's machine holds one syrup and four dyes. I am the one to check: Baikal, Duchesse, Buratino and Tarragon, twenty-five rubles a sample. Finish each one and remember it.
quest.soda_science.tell.log: Four bottles, a hundred rubles and a slight hiccup. They do taste different, I know that for certain now. Report to Galina before I forget which one was green.
quest.soda_science.done: Hypothesis disproved: four syrups. I got my hundred rubles back and a kefir as hazard pay. I think the Laboratory now lists me as an instrument.
line.zotova_galina.sodalab_ask.1: You go to the club, don't you? There is a machine there with four sodas. I need an independent taster.
line.zotova_galina.sodalab_ask.2: Working hypothesis: it is all one syrup, and only the dye differs.
line.zotova_galina.sodalab_ask.4: I am biased, I have read the ingredients. Drink all four, one at a time, and report.
line.zotova_galina.sodalab_ask.5: The laboratory will cover expenses. That is to say, I will.
line.zotova_galina.sodalab_wait.1: The sample is incomplete. Four specimens, each to the bottom. A sip does not count as science.
line.zotova_galina.sodalab_tell.1: All four? Then I am taking the minutes. Go on.
line.hero.sodalab_tell.2: Baikal is like pine, Duchesse is sticky. Buratino stings the tongue, and Tarragon is just green.
line.zotova_galina.sodalab_tell.3: "Green" is not a flavour, but it goes in the minutes. Hypothesis disproved: four syrups.
line.zotova_galina.sodalab_tell.4: Lev claims he can tell them apart with his eyes shut. Next we test Lev.
line.zotova_galina.sodalab_tell.5: Here are a hundred rubles, as budgeted, and a kefir as hazard pay. Those are the rules.
quest.hot_corn.title: A hot cob
quest.hot_corn.desc: Valentina Guseva boils corn in the square. One of her oldest customers no longer makes it that far.
quest.hot_corn.ask.log: In the Academgorodok's square, under a yellow umbrella, Valentina Guseva sells boiled corn. Eleven to six, every day. She looks at me as if she has an errand in mind.
quest.hot_corn.buy.log: Valentina wants a cob taken to Ivan Korneev, Nina's husband. It is her present, but I am the one who buys it: fifteen rubles, at the same cart. She promised to settle up when I come back.
quest.hot_corn.carry.log: The cob is in my pocket, warm through the napkin. Ivan Korneev lives with Nina in the Academgorodok. Up at six, fishing off the beach in the mornings, out in the yard or at home by day. The main thing is not to eat it on the way.
quest.hot_corn.give_cob.obj: Take the cob to Ivan Korneev
quest.hot_corn.tell.log: Ivan got his cob and approved. He gave me a few words about the salt and one promise to pass on to Valentina. She is at the cart until six.
quest.hot_corn.done: Valentina gave me back my fifteen rubles, five on top, and one more cob, this one for me. Ivan promised to come by when the fish stop biting. She says that means never, and I think she is pleased.
line.guseva_valentina.corn_errand.1: You're walking back and forth anyway. Take a cob to Vanya Korneev, Nina's husband.
line.guseva_valentina.corn_errand.2: He used to come every day. Now it's the fishing rod from dawn, and his legs won't carry him as far as the square.
line.guseva_valentina.corn_errand.4: You, for now. The pot doesn't sell on credit. Come back and we'll settle up.
line.guseva_valentina.corn_till.1: Buy the cob first. A present is a present, and the till is the till.
line.guseva_valentina.corn_hurry.1: Off you go while it's hot. Vanya will never forgive me a cold cob.
line.korneev_ivan.corn_handover.1: From Valya? Still hot. So you walked fast and didn't take a bite on the way. I respect that.
line.korneev_ivan.corn_handover.2: I fitted the wheel on that cart of hers. It still squeaks. She says that's it saying hello.
line.korneev_ivan.corn_handover.3: Tell her the salt is just right. And that I'll come by. When the fish stop biting.
line.korneev_ivan.corn_nocob.1: Corn from Valya, you say? And your hands are empty. I understand: a long road, a good cob.
line.korneev_ivan.corn_eaten.1: The cob is gone, there's only the core left. Mind you tell Valya.
line.guseva_valentina.corn_report.1: Well, how's Vanya? Did he eat it? What did he say?
line.hero.corn_report.2: The salt is just right. And he'll come by when the fish stop biting.
line.guseva_valentina.corn_report.3: Never, then. Well, let him fish. He mentioned the salt, that's what matters.
line.guseva_valentina.corn_report.4: Here's your fifteen back, and five on top for the legwork. And take a cob, this one is for you.
quest.lab_lunch.title: An independent expert
quest.lab_lunch.desc: Vika Li has not had time for lunch in three years. She has heard two opinions of the fish soup at the Chaika diner, and neither is her own.
quest.lab_lunch.ask.log: Vika Li, a lab assistant, lives in the Academgorodok. By day she is at the laboratory; she is in the yard before nine, after half past five and at weekends. She looks as if she has a job for me.
quest.lab_lunch.eat.log: Vika wants an honest word on the fish soup at the Chaika. It is the lunch car across the street from the lower cable car station, open till evening. The soup costs forty rubles. Order at the counter and eat it to the bottom: a half-eaten bowl does not count.
quest.lab_lunch.eat_soup.obj: Order the fish soup at the Chaika and finish it
quest.lab_lunch.tell.log: The bowl is empty. Cod, potatoes, dill, and the spoon would not stop by itself. I have a finding; it only has to reach Vika.
quest.lab_lunch.done: The soup is found good, and Misha is found to be a man who dislikes dill. I got my lunch money back and a chocolate bar. Vika says she will go herself on Saturday. We shall see.
line.li_vika.lunch_ask.1: Did you have lunch today? Lucky you. I didn't. Third year running.
line.li_vika.lunch_ask.2: The diner by the lower station makes a fish soup. Kei says it is the best thing in town. Misha says the worst. They have been at it for two weeks.
line.li_vika.lunch_ask.3: I need an independent expert. Go, eat a bowl and tell me honestly.
line.hero.lunch_ask.4: I'll go. I'll tell it as it is.
line.li_vika.lunch_ask.5: To the bottom, mind. Nobody draws conclusions from two spoonfuls.
line.li_vika.lunch_wait.1: Not eaten yet? Then say nothing. I like a clean experiment. The diner is across the street from the lower station.
line.li_vika.lunch_tell.1: I can see by your face that you ate. Well? Best or worst?
line.hero.lunch_tell.2: It's good. Cod, potatoes, a lot of dill. The bowl is empty.
line.li_vika.lunch_tell.3: A lot of dill. That settles it: Kei is right, and Misha simply dislikes dill. Noted.
line.li_vika.lunch_tell.4: Here, that is for the soup. And take the chocolate, it is my usual lunch. On Saturday I'll go myself. With a spoon and without the lab coat.
quest.night_signal.title: A light on the bluff
quest.night_signal.desc: Valiev the engineer has worked out on paper that a small light up by the club can be seen from his window. He does not quite trust the paper.
quest.night_signal.ask.log: Rustam Valiev, an engineer at the Laboratory, lives in the Academgorodok. They say he spends his evenings looking out of his window at the upland. On weekdays he is out after half past five, at weekends all day.
quest.night_signal.signal.log: Rustam needs a light on the edge of the upland. Ogawa sells head lamps at the club, forty rubles. Then out to the upper cable car station, better after dark, and put it on there. If it is already on my head, take it off and put it on again: a signal has to appear. L switches it on and off.
quest.night_signal.reach_station.obj: Go out to the upper cable car station
quest.night_signal.tell.log: Stood by the upper station with a lamp on my forehead. The town below glowed and gave no sign of having noticed me. Tell Rustam: he goes to bed at half past eleven, tomorrow will do too.
quest.night_signal.done: Rustam saw one point of light above the bluff and honestly cannot say whether it was me. He counts the experiment a success all the same. I got my forty rubles back for the lamp, and fruit candies in place of a bonus.
line.valiev_rustam.signal_ask.1: You get up to the club now and then, don't you? I need someone with a lamp and no unnecessary questions.
line.valiev_rustam.signal_ask.3: One is fine. From my window I can see the edge of the upland, where the upper cable car station stands. By my figures a small light there ought to be visible. I want to check with my own eyes.
line.valiev_rustam.signal_ask.4: You will need a head lamp. Ogawa keeps them at the club. Once it is dark, go out to the upper station and put it on there.
line.valiev_rustam.signal_ask.5: I will be at the window. Come and tell me afterwards, and we will compare notes.
line.valiev_rustam.signal_wait.1: No light so far, and I am watching. The lamp is at Ogawa's, the place is the upper station, the time is after dark.
line.valiev_rustam.signal_tell.1: Well, report. Were you up there?
line.hero.signal_tell.2: I was. I stood by the upper station with the lamp on my forehead.
line.valiev_rustam.signal_tell.3: I saw one point of light above the bluff. Either it was you, or something glinted at the station. From a single observation I cannot honestly tell.
line.valiev_rustam.signal_tell.5: It succeeded. The figures said it should be visible. The eye says something is visible. For a first run that is decent agreement.
line.valiev_rustam.signal_tell.6: Keep the lamp. I will cover the cost of the equipment. And take the candies, they are in place of a bonus.
quest.tent_neighbours.title: Neighbours across the counter
quest.tent_neighbours.desc: Aslan Khuazhev knows everything about his cheese. What the town eats besides cheese he does not know at all, and he cannot leave his counter.
quest.tent_neighbours.ask.log: There is a red and white tent by the club's door. Aslan Khuazhev sells Adyghe cheese in it from ten to eight, every day but Monday. He says hello as if the table were already laid.
quest.tent_neighbours.hear_aslan.obj: Talk to Aslan at the tent by the club
quest.tent_neighbours.taste.log: Aslan is deciding what to bring next season and wants to know what his neighbours feed people. I am to do the eating for him. Corn from Valentina in the Academgorodok's square, fifteen rubles, eleven to six. A pie from the machine at the upper cable car station, eighteen. Pancakes at the Chaika diner by the lower station, thirty-five. All of it to the last bite: he will not count a nibble.
quest.tent_neighbours.eat_pie.obj: Eat a pie from the vending machine
quest.tent_neighbours.eat_pancakes.obj: Order the pancakes at the Chaika and finish them
quest.tent_neighbours.tell.log: Corn, pie and pancakes, all inside me. Sixty-eight rubles and not one thought of food until tomorrow. Time to report to Aslan before he closes the tent.
quest.tent_neighbours.tell_aslan.obj: Tell Aslan what the town eats
quest.tent_neighbours.done: Aslan will bring more of the smoked kind and a soft cheese to go with pancakes. I got my lunch money back and a round of cheese, handed over with a toast. The toast was longer than the lunch.
line.khuazhev_aslan.tent_ask.1: A guest at the tent is a feast already. Come closer, my friend, I have a matter more important than trade.
line.khuazhev_aslan.tent_ask.2: In winter I go home for stock. I want to know what this town eats when it is not eating my cheese.
line.khuazhev_aslan.tent_ask.3: I cannot take a step from this counter. Try three things for me: Valentina's corn, a pie from the machine at the station, and the pancakes at the diner down below.
line.khuazhev_aslan.tent_ask.5: Only eat to the end, as at a friend's table. He who takes one bite and runs has understood nothing.
line.khuazhev_aslan.tent_wait.1: Not tried them all yet? No hurry. Corn in the square, the pie at the station, pancakes down by the cable car. A hungry guest tells a poor story.
line.khuazhev_aslan.tent_report.1: I see it in your eyes: here is a man well fed. Tell me, what do my neighbours serve?
line.hero.tent_report.2: The corn is hot and salty. The pancakes come with sour cream, they're good. The pie is a pie.
line.khuazhev_aslan.tent_report.3: Valentina does not spare the salt, I respect that. Pancakes with sour cream: so they love their dairy here. But a pie out of an iron box, ah.
line.khuazhev_aslan.tent_report.4: It is decided. I bring more of the smoked, and a soft cheese for the pancakes. With the box I will not compete: I pity it enough already.
line.khuazhev_aslan.tent_report.5: So let us drink... no, let us eat. To the one who eats honestly and tells the truth. Take this round, and take the money for your lunch: a guest does not pay for another man's errand.
quest.owner_supper.title: Supper for the owner
quest.owner_supper.desc: Kenji Ogawa sits in his booth from noon till two at night. Without supper, it seems.
quest.owner_supper.back.log: The club's owner sits in his booth from noon till two at night. I have never once seen him eat. I'll go back to the club and ask.
quest.owner_supper.ask.log: I'm at the club. The booth window glows the same as it did by day. Ask the owner whether he has eaten today.
quest.owner_supper.buy.log: He hasn't. He asked for a cheese braid and a bottle of Baikal. Aslan sells the braids at the tent by the club door, Tuesday to Sunday, until eight in the evening. The Baikal is in the machine in the hall. Fifty rubles for the lot.
quest.owner_supper.get_cheese.obj: Buy a cheese braid from Aslan by the club
quest.owner_supper.get_soda.obj: Get a Baikal from the machine in the club
quest.owner_supper.bring.log: I have the cheese and the Baikal. Take them to the booth window. The owner is there from noon till two at night, so it is hard to be late.
quest.owner_supper.give_cheese.obj: Take the cheese to the club's owner
quest.owner_supper.give_soda.obj: Take the Baikal to the club's owner
quest.owner_supper.done: The owner had his supper right at the window. I got sixty rubles and some bird feed. Not payment, he said, just change.
line.owner.supper_ask.1: Been sitting here since noon. Not a step from this spot till two at night.
line.owner.supper_ask.3: Supper is out there. And I am in here.
line.owner.supper_ask.4: Aslan's tent is by the door. Get me a cheese braid from him. And a Baikal from the machine.
line.owner.supper_ask.6: Don't run. Cheese doesn't go cold.
line.owner.supper_wait.1: Take your time. I'm here till two.
line.owner.supper_thanks.1: A braid. Smells of smoke, the way it should.
line.owner.supper_thanks.2: The sun I can feel on the back of my neck. Hunger I never notice until somebody reminds me.
line.owner.supper_thanks.4: Here. It isn't payment, it's your change. And the feed is for the birds, it's their supper time too.
line.owner.supper_after.1: The tea's run out again. But there is still some cheese. A good evening.
quest.overdue_journal.title: The overdue reader
quest.overdue_journal.desc: Olya, the Academgorodok librarian, has waited half a year for one magazine. She is too shy to remind the reader.
quest.overdue_journal.ask.log: Olya from the club, the one who scrolls the forums, works at the Academgorodok library: Wednesday to Saturday, ten to three. Something is bothering her, and for once it is not the forum.
quest.overdue_journal.visit.log: Lev Zotov, a physicist from the Laboratory, borrowed the magazine "Cosmos and Us" in spring and never brought it back. Olya set out to remind him three times and said hello three times. I will ask. On weekdays he works until five; in the evening and at weekends he is around the Academgorodok yard.
quest.overdue_journal.ask_lev.obj: Ask Lev Zotov about the magazine
quest.overdue_journal.buy.log: The magazine is found: since April it has been under the leg of an interferometer, holding up half a year of measurements. It is not coming back. Lev gave me forty rubles for a fresh issue. The vending machine at the Academgorodok cable car station, the one with the pendulum, sells "Cosmos and Us".
quest.overdue_journal.return.log: I have the fresh issue. No cup rings on the cover, never been under an instrument. Take it to Olya: she is at the library Wednesday to Saturday, ten to three, and at the club in the evenings.
quest.overdue_journal.done: The new issue is on the shelf. The old one is entered as lent indefinitely, for the needs of science: Olya drew the column herself. I got a written-off copy of "Shores" and a chocolate bar from her desk drawer. I think I am a reader now too.
line.girl_b.overdue_ask.1: Listen, can I ask you something odd? There is a debt hanging over my library. Not mine, a reader's.
line.girl_b.overdue_ask.2: Lev Zotov, the physicist, borrowed "Cosmos and Us" in spring. And never brought it back.
line.girl_b.overdue_ask.4: I set out three times. He says "good afternoon" and I forget why I came over. Could you ask him, please?
line.girl_b.overdue_wait.1: On weekdays he is at the Laboratory until five, then he walks in the yard. Just don't say I am cross. I am not cross.
line.girl_b.overdue_hint.1: Buy a new one? The machine at the station has them, the one by the pendulum. But that is forty rubles, and now I feel awkward.
line.zotov_lev.overdue_admit.1: "Cosmos and Us"? I took it, I don't deny it. I read it with a pencil: there is an error in a formula on page fourteen.
line.zotov_lev.overdue_admit.2: Then a leg of the interferometer began to wobble. The magazine turned out to be exactly the right thickness.
line.zotov_lev.overdue_admit.4: Since April. It is a load-bearing structure now: pull it out and half a year of measurements is gone.
line.zotov_lev.overdue_admit.5: Here are forty rubles, buy her a fresh issue from the machine at the station. And tell Olya the old one is serving science.
line.girl_b.overdue_empty.1: And where is the magazine? Never mind, I will wait. I have waited half a year, I can wait a little more.
line.girl_b.overdue_back.1: A fresh issue? And no cup rings on the cover. But where is the old one?
line.hero.overdue_back.2: Under the leg of an interferometer. Lev says it is serving science.
line.girl_b.overdue_back.3: I will put it on the card: "lent indefinitely, for the needs of science". There is no such column, but I will draw one.
line.girl_b.overdue_back.4: Thank you. On my own I would have been setting out until I retired. Here, take these: a written-off copy of "Shores" and a chocolate bar from my desk drawer.
quest.autumn_count.title: The autumn count
quest.autumn_count.desc: Sorokin has taken up the bird count he dropped years ago. His knees are the same as before, so the walking is mine.
quest.autumn_count.kit.log: There was a notebook page in the bag of feed. Small, even handwriting: “Resuming the autumn count. Assistant with a feeder required. Sorokin.” Tanya sells feeders at the grocery, eighty rubles. Or I fetch mine from wherever I left it.
quest.autumn_count.get_feeder.obj: Get hold of a bird feeder
quest.autumn_count.brief.log: I have a feeder. Sorokin sits on a bench in the Academgorodok's square from eight till half past twelve and from half past two till half past six. I'll ask what an assistant's duties are.
quest.autumn_count.hear_sorokin.obj: Come to Sorokin with the feeder
quest.autumn_count.post.log: The job is this: put the feeder up right here in the Academgorodok, on level open ground, and fill it with peanuts. Peanuts precisely; Sorokin said it twice. If mine have run out, the grocery has them.
quest.autumn_count.fill_peanuts.obj: Put the feeder up in the Academgorodok and fill it with peanuts
quest.autumn_count.tally.log: The peanuts are in. Now step back twenty paces, crouch and count the landings: six are needed. And feed one great tit from the palm, to get a proper look at the black stripe down its breast. Birds feed by day; towards evening there is no point waiting.
quest.autumn_count.count_visits.obj: Count the landings on the feeder
quest.autumn_count.tame_tit.obj: Feed a great tit from the palm
quest.autumn_count.report.log: Six landings, and a great tit sat on my palm. I have the stripe on its breast by heart. Time to hand the data to Sorokin.
quest.autumn_count.done: My six landings and one great tit are in Sorokin's journal now, with two surnames under “observer”. He poured me some goldfinch mix and gave me a tit cake. The count, he said, is ours from now on.
line.sorokin_oleg.autumn_kit.1: You read my note? Then where is the feeder? A counter without a feeder is just a passer-by.
line.sorokin_oleg.autumn_brief.1: You have the feeder. Sit down, there is work.
line.sorokin_oleg.autumn_brief.2: Thirty autumns I kept a bird count, and then I dropped it. After the waxwing, dropping things became awkward.
line.sorokin_oleg.autumn_brief.3: It is called the autumn count. I hold it whenever there is someone to do the walking.
line.hero.autumn_brief.4: What do I have to do?
line.sorokin_oleg.autumn_brief.5: Be my legs. Put the feeder up here in the Academgorodok and fill it with the peanuts from my stock.
line.sorokin_oleg.autumn_brief.6: Step back twenty paces, crouch and count the landings. Six landings already make a sample.
line.sorokin_oleg.autumn_brief.7: And feed one great tit from your palm. I need its tie, and that can only be seen up close.
line.sorokin_oleg.autumn_brief.9: The black stripe down the breast: broad on the male, narrow on the female. Birds dress more strictly than people.
line.sorokin_oleg.autumn_wait.1: Peanuts, twenty paces, six landings, one great tit from the palm. And keep still: a counter should be duller than a tree stump.
line.hero.autumn_report.1: Six landings. And a great tit ate from my palm.
line.sorokin_oleg.autumn_report.2: Not a word about the tie. Write it in yourself, in this column here: I like to read data, not listen to it.
line.sorokin_oleg.autumn_report.3: So. Six landings, one great tit on the palm. For one sitting and one assistant, respectable.
line.sorokin_oleg.autumn_report.4: Thirty autumns I counted alone. With two, it turns out, the figures are more honest.
line.sorokin_oleg.autumn_report.5: Take the goldfinch mix and a tit cake. The goldfinches want to be in the journal too, and you know now how they are entered.
line.sorokin_oleg.tips_feeder_in_hand.1: You have the feeder already, that's half the job. Check you've got Olya's guide and Tanya's rowan, and then go north, past the hills.
line.sorokin_oleg.grove_after_dark.1: Don't go there in the dark. Waxwings sleep at night, and the wood past the hills is no easy walk even by day.
line.sorokin_oleg.grove_after_dark.2: Set off at first light and keep north, right through the town. In the morning birds are hungry, and bolder.
line.sorokin_oleg.rowan_till_dawn.1: It's dark, the waxwings are asleep. The rowan and the feeder can wait till morning, and so can you.
line.sorokin_oleg.rowan_till_dawn.2: At first light the first thing they look for is food. Be in the grove before them, with rowan in the feeder.
line.sorokin_oleg.count_by_lantern.1: No counting at night, the tits are asleep. In the morning: peanuts in the feeder, twenty paces, six landings and one tit from the palm.
line.sorokin_oleg.count_by_lantern.2: At your age I counted by lantern too. I counted one owl and a pair of wet boots.
line.sorokin_oleg.kit_from_dasha.1: Dasha Kimura says you counted five birds at a feeder for her. So you know how to set one up.
line.sorokin_oleg.kit_from_dasha.2: Now I need it with you. Take back the one you set up, or buy a new one from Tanya at the grocery.
line.lange_pyotr.pier_dawn_dusk.1: Night fishing's for those who know the water. You want the dawn or the dusk: that's when fish get bolder.
line.lange_pyotr.pier_no_worms.1: No worms. Maggots would do, but I'd take worms: Tanya at the grocery, fifteen for ten.
line.lange_pyotr.pier_no_worms.2: Then back to the pier, by the piles.
line.korneev_ivan.corn_paper_boy.1: Ah, the paper boy. I solved that evening's problem, mate in three. Nina still says you saved her from me.
line.korneev_ivan.corn_paper_boy.2: And now a cob from Valya, still hot. Tell her the salt's just right, and I'll drop by once the fish stop biting.
line.korneeva_nina.paper_after_dark.1: It's dark already and Vanya still has no chess problem. The fair square's down by the sea, with the news stall. I'm not rushing you, I'm reminding you.
line.kimura_dasha.feeder_no_data_night.1: No data at night: the birds are asleep, not voting. Put feed in a feeder and come and count in the morning, I need five visits.
line.sato_yuki.crows_roost_night.1: The crows are asleep now. All together, in one big tree. Papa says they tell each other who fed them.
line.sato_yuki.crows_roost_night.2: Tomorrow throw them some food, three times. And wait for the present, they're not quick.
line.belov_misha.magpie_crow_friend.1: Word is the crows already bring you presents. So you've got connections.
line.belov_misha.magpie_crow_friend.2: Use them. Three finds will do: something dropped, something buried, something brought to you.
line.orlova_tanya.rowan_guide_left.1: Rowan, yes. Feeder, yes. That leaves the guide: Olya has it at the library, right on her desk.
line.orlova_tanya.rowan_guide_left.2: Sorokin says without a guide every bird in the wood is grey.
line.valiev_rustam.signal_lamp_ready.1: You've got the lamp already, I see. Once it's dark, go up to the upper station and put it on there.
line.valiev_rustam.signal_lamp_ready.2: I'll be at the window. I even wiped the glass, first time since spring.
line.nishimura_aya.views_low_light.1: See this light? Low sun, long shadows. The promenade, the starlings, the rowan wood: look now, while it lasts.
line.khuazhev_aslan.taste_corn_courier.1: You're the one who carried Valentina's cob to Ivan? She told me, praised you half the day.
line.khuazhev_aslan.taste_corn_courier.2: So you know the way. Corn in the square, a pie at the station, pancakes down by the cable car, and all of it to the last bite.
line.kid_girl.sparrow_bedtime.1: The sparrows are asleep already. Mum says birds go to bed even before me. Tomorrow I'll watch again.
line.zotova_galina.sodalab_pocket.1: The Baikal is in your pocket, not in my record. A sample counts once it's drunk: all four, to the bottom.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_wait_hint.1: Rowan in the feeder, right there in the grove, and stay nearby. A waxwing looks first at who's sitting close, and only then at the treat.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_wait_snow.1: When one lands on the feeder, crouch and hold out your palm with rowan. I once sat half a day like that in the snow, the best half day of my life.
line.sorokin_oleg.autumn_wait_hint.1: Peanuts in the feeder here in the yard, then twenty paces back. The tits will come first, and the boldest one you feed from the palm.
line.sorokin_oleg.autumn_wait_sandwich.1: Six landings and one tit from the palm. Once I counted with a sandwich in my hand, and the tits decided they were the ones doing the count.
line.korneeva_nina.paper_wait_hint.1: The fair square's down by the sea, with the news stall. Get the evening one with the chess problem, Vanya won't have any other.
line.korneeva_nina.paper_wait_vanya.1: Vanya's asked three times where the paper is. I told him you're on your way, down by the sea, so don't let me down.
line.lange_pyotr.cheese_wait_hint.1: Up to the club, by cable car. Cheese tent by the door. One smoked braid.
line.lange_pyotr.cheese_wait_gull.1: A gull sat on my net this morning and looked at me the way I'm looking at you. Cheese, by the club.
line.lange_pyotr.catch_wait_hint.1: End of the pier, by the piles. Let the float go right under, then strike: sooner is too soon, later is too late.
line.lange_pyotr.catch_wait_nets.1: I'd come along, but nets don't mend themselves. Pier, worm, and don't leave till it bites.
line.kimura_dasha.feeder_wait_hint.1: Any feeder will do. Ask Tanya for the suet cake, the one for great tits: they can't resist it, and pigeons won't even look at it.
line.kimura_dasha.feeder_wait_dishes.1: Vika's already washing the dishes in her head, I can see it on her face. I only need five visits.
line.sato_yuki.crow_wait_hint.1: Crows walk about by the sea and in the fields. Throw them food, three times. They watch who's kind.
line.sato_yuki.crow_wait_drawing.1: I drew a crow, without the button, so she won't be hurt. You keep feeding them, and pick up the present when they bring it.
line.belov_misha.magpie_wait_hint.1: Magpies in the gardens, crows on the beach, jackdaws on the roofs, and they all hide things. Pick up what's lying about and dig where they've buried.
line.belov_misha.magpie_wait_nuts.1: Just in case, I counted the nuts on my workbench. All there, which is suspicious. Three finds will do me.
line.nishimura_aya.views_wait_hint.1: The promenade's down by the sea, and the starlings are over the sea in the evenings. The rowan wood is far, past the northern hills: go there with plenty of day ahead.
line.nishimura_aya.views_wait_gull.1: Today on the island I spent all day painting one gull, and it never landed. Three places, take your time.
line.valiev_rustam.signal_wait_hint.1: Ogawa sells head lamps, at the club, and the upper station is right by the club. Put it on there once it's dark.
line.valiev_rustam.signal_wait_window.1: Last night I watched from the window all evening. Three stars, one satellite and a neighbour with a cigarette, but not you.
line.orlova_tanya.rowan_doorway.1: Come in. You've got the face Sorokin gets when he's thinking about his waxwings.
line.girl_b.north_send_off.1: Off north already? That's a long way. If you see a waxwing, tell Sorokin first, and then me.
line.kimura_dasha.tally_stump.1: Sitting like a stump and moving your lips, so you're counting for Sorokin. Respect, I can't do that even in an exam.
line.sorokin_oleg.views_small_town.1: Aya told me you looked at the town from the rowan wood. Small and quiet, she says.
line.sorokin_oleg.views_small_town.2: From a bird's height every town looks like that. I think that's why birds put up with them.
line.korneeva_nina.cob_for_vanya.1: That's for Vanya, from Valya? I can smell it.
line.korneeva_nina.cob_for_vanya.2: After three he's usually on the bench, if he's not by the sea. Tell him to share with me.
line.lange_pyotr.crows_herring_crate.1: Feeding the crows? They pinch herring out of my crate. Tell them I see everything.
line.sato_yuki.crows_from_bench.1: I'm watching from here, it's not scary from here. That big one took the button, I recognised her.
line.belov_misha.rustam_window.1: Rustam's having supper at the window tonight, says he's waiting for a signal. You wouldn't be the signal, would you?
line.li_vika.pigeon_counts_twice.1: Counting Dasha's birds? A pigeon is a bird too. Please write it down twice.
line.zotov_lev.soda_eyes_shut.1: Galina sent you tasting? I can tell Baikal from Tarragon with my eyes shut. Just don't tell her, she'll test it.
line.zotova_galina.interferometer_file.1: A new magazine for Olya? Lev told me. The interferometer's leg could have been filed down, you know.
Aslan sent you? He praises my corn and has never once tried it. Eat for two.
line.nao.supper_smoke.1: Getting the owner's supper? The tent's right here. It smells of smoke, like a fire that isn't there.
line.khuazhev_aslan.braid_for_fisher.1: A braid for a fisherman? Guessed right, didn't I? Fishermen always take the smoked one, so that something in life isn't fish.
line.korneeva_nina.paper_rook.1: Vanya solved his problem before supper. Now he walks about proud, looking for someone to show it to.
line.korneeva_nina.paper_rook.2: I told him: show the boy, he brought the paper. So brace yourself, there's a rook sacrifice in it.
line.korneeva_nina.paper_postman.1: A paper for Vanya, a cob for Vanya. You're our postman now, only you deliver hot food too.
line.korneeva_nina.paper_postman.2: I'll tell him to bring you something in return. A chess problem, at least.
line.sato_yuki.crow_swap_feather.1: I left a juice bottle cap on the bench for the crow. In the morning it was gone.
line.sato_yuki.crow_swap_feather.2: And yesterday there was a feather there. Black and shiny. So we're swapping fair and square.
line.sato_yuki.crow_magpie_uncle.1: Uncle Misha says you collected the magpies' finds for him. You must know every bird there is.
line.lange_pyotr.braid_three_days.1: Made the braid last three days. A bit at a time, after the sea.
line.lange_pyotr.braid_three_days.2: Now I know who to ask. Not too often, or I'll go soft.
line.lange_pyotr.angler_spoon_dawn.1: Well then, angler. The spoon is for hunters: cast it off the end of the pier at dawn or dusk, the garfish run there.
line.lange_pyotr.angler_spoon_dawn.2: Sell the small fry to Tanya at the grocery. The big ones they'll fry for you at the Chaika, fifteen rubles.
line.lange_pyotr.angler_dusk_now.1: The light's low and you're talking to me. At this hour an angler is on the pier, not at a bench.
line.kimura_dasha.feeder_table_rows.1: Your feeder is still standing in the yard. Mornings I keep a table: tits, sparrows, and one magpie that only looked.
line.kimura_dasha.feeder_table_rows.2: Vika says it's no longer a bet, it's an obsession. She says it over the sink.
line.kimura_dasha.feeder_two_counts.1: Sorokin says you counted six landings for him. Five for me, six for him: our yard has a scientific school of its own now.
line.belov_misha.key_on_string.1: I wear the key on a string round my neck now. Like in first grade.
line.belov_misha.key_on_string.2: And the magpie lands on my windowsill every evening. Checking I haven't taken the apology back.
line.nishimura_aya.new_sketchbook.1: I've started a new sketchbook. On the first page, the town from far off, from your words.
line.nishimura_aya.new_sketchbook.2: It's crooked, but honest. The island can wait a while, it's patient.
line.kid_girl.sparrow_named_kuzya.1: I named the sparrow Kuzya. He lives by the club door. I say hello and he doesn't fly away.
line.hero.sparrow_named_kuzya.2: How do you know it's him?
line.kid_girl.sparrow_named_kuzya.3: He looks at me in a special way. As if he knows me too.
line.kid_girl.sparrow_crumbs_door.1: You've got bird feed? Scatter a little by the door for my sparrow. Mum won't give me money for the machine.
line.zotova_galina.green_confirmed.1: After your report I bought a Tarragon. It really is just green.
line.zotova_galina.green_confirmed.2: I tested Lev as well. The results are classified, at his request.
line.zotova_galina.two_favours_lev.1: You sorted out Olya's magazine and disproved my hypothesis. Our household is in your debt, Lev especially.
line.guseva_valentina.wheel_oiled.1: Vanya came to the cart himself, you know. Says the fish stopped biting. He's fibbing, of course, but I didn't argue.
line.guseva_valentina.wheel_oiled.2: Oiled my wheel while he was at it. It doesn't squeak now, and it's gone rather quiet.
line.korneev_ivan.cart_visit_secret.1: I went over to Valya's. Between us, the fish never stopped biting. Don't tell her.
line.korneev_ivan.cart_visit_secret.2: Her corn's better than I remembered. Or I've got hungrier.
line.li_vika.saturday_plan.1: I've put the fish soup in my plan for Saturday. Under “aim of the experiment” I wrote: have lunch.
line.li_vika.saturday_plan.2: Misha took offence, but he's promised to try it without dill. That's a result too.
line.valiev_rustam.brighter_lamp_calc.1: I ran the figures again. With a brighter lamp the dot would show even in drizzle. But that's another experiment.
line.valiev_rustam.brighter_lamp_calc.2: And I don't draw the curtain any more. I've got used to watching the edge of the upland in the evenings.
line.valiev_rustam.second_dot.1: Last night a dot flickered above the bluff again. Not you? Then at last I have a control observation.
line.khuazhev_aslan.letter_to_brother.1: I've already written to my brother: we're bringing a soft cheese for the pancakes. He asks who gave the advice.
line.khuazhev_aslan.letter_to_brother.2: I told him: an honest man, and a well-fed one. I keep no other advisers.
line.girl_b.fresh_issue_twice.1: The new “Cosmos and Us” has been borrowed twice already. Both times it came back on time, I hardly knew what to do.
line.girl_b.fresh_issue_twice.2: Lev says hello first now. And now I remember why I came over.
line.zotov_lev.load_bearing_reading.1: The interferometer stands level, the magazine holds. Galina says it's the most useful thing I've read all year.
line.zotov_lev.load_bearing_reading.2: I did write to them about the error on page fourteen. A letter, to the editors.
line.sorokin_oleg.bluetit_at_dawn.1: This morning I sat by your feeder. Eight landings and one blue tit: you haven't seen her yet, but she has seen you.
line.sorokin_oleg.bluetit_at_dawn.2: Autumn is long. Come by whenever your legs are free.
line.owner.supper_where.1: The braid is at Aslan's tent by the door, till eight, not on Mondays. The Baikal is in the machine, here in the hall.
line.owner.supper_slow_time.1: Without supper time goes slower. Don't hurry, but don't forget: cheese and a Baikal.
line.kid_girl.sparrow_palm_hint.1: The sparrows sit by the club door. You have to crouch, hold out your hand with feed and not move at all.
line.kid_girl.sparrow_count_four.1: Today I counted the sparrows by the door. Four. And not one said hello.
line.zotova_galina.sodalab_where.1: The machine is in the club, twenty-five rubles a bottle. Baikal, Duchesse, Buratino, Tarragon, each to the bottom.
line.zotova_galina.sodalab_empty_rows.1: I've already set up the record. Four rows, all of them still empty.
line.li_vika.lunch_where.1: The fish soup is forty rubles, you order at the counter. The Chaika is across the street from the lower cable car station.
line.li_vika.lunch_borscht_debate.1: Kei and Misha were at it again from first thing this morning. I need a verdict before they move on to borscht.
line.khuazhev_aslan.taste_hours.1: Valentina's at her cart till six, the Chaika down below till evening. And the pie in the station's machine is always waiting.
line.khuazhev_aslan.taste_imagined.1: Three times today I've pictured those pancakes. Eat them soon, before I make them up myself.
line.girl_b.lev_bench_hint.1: In the evenings Lev sits on a bench in the yard, from half past five till seven. Weekends too.
line.girl_b.ficus_instead.1: I set out myself again. Got as far as the door and remembered the ficus needed watering.
line.clerk.soda_palette.1: Baikal, Duchesse, Buratino, Tarragon. Dark brown, pale yellow, amber, green. A good palette.
line.owner.lamp_batteries.1: A lamp? This light you may touch. It runs on batteries, not on its own.
line.guy_b.owner_ate_film.1: Saw the owner eating cheese at the booth window. Watched it like a film. Even the ventilation hummed quieter.
line.girl_a.sparrow_retold.1: Sonya has told me three times now about the sparrow that came by itself. I listen to the end every time, I even leave my program.
line.kid_boy.sparrow_no_hello.1: Sonya says a sparrow said hello to her. I said that doesn't happen. Now she won't say hello to me.
line.girl_b.aya_atlas.1: Aya came in and took out the atlas of the surroundings. She says she wants to find where you stood when you looked at the town.
line.orlova_tanya.rowan_again.1: Sorokin bought dried rowan again. He says if one came, the others may find the way too.
line.nao.aslan_pancake_talk.1: Aslan tells everyone about the pancakes with sour cream. Even me, and I just stand by the door.
line.zotov_lev.soda_mixed_up.1: I told Baikal from Tarragon, as promised. But I mixed up Duchesse and Buratino. Galina put it in the record.
line.sato_kei.soup_measured.1: Vika says the independent expert sided with me. I thought so: soup, like light, has to be measured yourself, not by Misha.
line.belov_misha.two_lamps.1: Rustam wants to repeat the experiment with two lamps. I think I'm the one holding the second.
line.li_vika.dishes_traitors.1: Day after day of dishes. And the pigeons still won't come to your feeder. Traitors.
line.sorokin_oleg.magpie_faces.1: I hear Misha Belov apologised to the magpie. Quite right: magpies remember faces longer than people do.
line.guseva_valentina.cheese_for_salt.1: Aslan sent me a round of cheese. For the salt, he says. So you told him the truth about my corn.
line.korneev_ivan.cheese_for_petya.1: Petya says you went up the hill to get him cheese. Nobody's brought him anything in twenty years.
line.korneeva_nina.yuki_talks_crows.1: Yuki's not afraid of the crows any more. She sits on her bench and talks to them, the way I talk to Tanya.
line.kimura_dasha.tit_row_monday.1: A great tit! Go on, sit down. You've been in my table since Monday.
line.kimura_dasha.pigeon_from_vika.1: A pigeon. Did Vika send you? Tell her you don't count.
line.kimura_dasha.flypast_void.1: A fly-past doesn't count. Land, and then we'll talk.
line.kimura_dasha.bird_by_the_book.1: Hello, bird. What are you, by the book? Fine, I'll put you down as "cute".
line.sato_yuki.crow_soon_fed.1: Oh, a crow. I'm not scared, I'm just sitting. Someone's going to feed you soon, I know who.
line.sato_yuki.button_suits_you.1: Hello, crow. You can keep the button, it suits you better.
line.sato_yuki.black_cousin.1: You're all black. You must be her cousin? You look just like her, only not grey.
line.sato_yuki.shout_from_above.1: Shouting from up there isn't fair, I can't see you. Come down and I'll look.
line.sato_yuki.not_too_close.1: Hi. I'm not scared of you. Just don't come too close, okay?
line.lange_pyotr.gull_try_pier.1: A gull. No fish here. Try the pier, there's a lad with a rod. Maybe he'll get lucky.
line.lange_pyotr.cormorant_ate_more.1: A cormorant. You again. You ate more this morning than I caught.
line.lange_pyotr.net_is_work.1: Leave the net alone. That's not food, that's work.
line.lange_pyotr.weather_without_you.1: Shout away. I know the weather without you.
line.lange_pyotr.counting_meshes.1: Sit. Quietly, though, I'm counting meshes.
line.belov_misha.key_under_shirt.1: A magpie. The key's on a string, under my shirt. You can stop looking at me like that.
line.belov_misha.confess_magpie.1: Well then, magpie, confess: where's the key? Fine, say nothing. I've got an investigator.
line.belov_misha.not_earthed.1: A jackdaw. Sit on the wire if you like, you're allowed: you're not earthed.
line.belov_misha.approach_no_landing.1: Nice approach. Only I don't see a landing.
line.belov_misha.nothing_shiny.1: Hi. Nothing shiny on me, honestly. I checked myself.
line.nishimura_aya.starling_messenger.1: A starling. Your lot are over the sea in the evenings, aren't they? Then you will see the town before my messenger does.
line.nishimura_aya.gull_sits_now.1: A gull, and it sits. On the island not one would land, and here, where I have only a pencil, it sits.
line.nishimura_aya.vermilion_drop.1: A bullfinch. Like a drop of vermilion. Stay there, I only need the breast.
line.nishimura_aya.wings_already.1: Stay on the page. All right, go, I have the wings already.
line.nishimura_aya.head_to_the_left.1: Stay like that. No, the head a little to the left. There, thank you.
line.zotova_galina.copper_sulphate.1: A blue tit. The colour of copper sulphate, without impurities.
line.zotova_galina.four_bottles_boy.1: Bird, if you see a young man at the club with four bottles, do not distract him. He is working for science.
line.zotova_galina.moving_source.1: I hear you, I hear you. High frequency, moving source.
line.zotova_galina.no_bread_crossword.1: Hello. I have no bread on me, I am sorry. Only a crossword.
line.zotov_lev.rook_referee.1: A rook. You have the look of a referee. I have already sent my letter to the editors, there is no need to stare.
line.zotov_lev.pendulum_pigeon.1: A pigeon. Nodding like a pendulum. Period, by eye, half a second.
line.zotov_lev.students_shout.1: Calling from above. Students do that too, and to the same effect.
line.zotov_lev.came_first.1: Sit with me. Galina says I am always late. Today I came first, and nobody saw.
line.korneeva_nina.pigeon_from_fair.1: Pigeon, are you from the fair square? You didn't see a boy with a paper down there?
line.korneeva_nina.sparrow_news.1: A sparrow. Go on, tell me what's new at the grocery. I haven't popped in to see Tanya yet today.
line.korneeva_nina.tell_me_properly.1: Listen to you shouting. Come down and tell me properly what's going on down there.
line.korneeva_nina.vanya_in_paper.1: Sit with me. Vanya's got his nose in the paper, there's no talking to him now.
line.korneev_ivan.cob_finished.1: Looking for corn? Too late, I finished it the same day. Down to the last kernel.
line.korneev_ivan.heron_colleague.1: A heron. A colleague. Nothing biting for you either, I'll bet.
line.korneev_ivan.see_the_fish.1: Flying high. I bet you can see where the fish are from up there.
line.korneev_ivan.good_company.1: Sit down, sit down. No crumbs, but good company.
line.valiev_rustam.not_the_signal.1: Something flickered. No, a bird. Signal not counted.
line.valiev_rustam.fastest_design.1: A peregrine. The fastest design in town, and it's sitting next to me.
line.valiev_rustam.good_stabilisation.1: Calling in flight and not wandering off course. Good stabilisation.
line.valiev_rustam.sits_level.1: You sit level, true as a spirit level. Good bird.
line.guseva_valentina.hear_you_now.1: A sparrow. Vanya oiled my wheel, and now I can hear you instead of the cart.
line.guseva_valentina.one_kernel.1: Sparrow, the corn's not for you, it's salted. Well, one kernel.
line.guseva_valentina.warm_by_the_pot.1: Come to warm up? The pot gives off heat, sit closer.
line.khuazhev_aslan.sonya_kuzya.1: A sparrow! You're Sonya's, I know. She calls you Kuzya, she's told everyone.
line.khuazhev_aslan.braids_counted.1: Crow, don't look at the cheese like that. The braids are counted, my mother counted them.
line.khuazhev_aslan.see_my_guest.1: Flying down to the cable car? Have a look whether my guest is finishing his pancakes.
line.khuazhev_aslan.cannot_haggle.1: Hey, who's shouting up there? Come down, my friend. You can't haggle from up there.
line.khuazhev_aslan.feathered_guest.1: Sit, sit. Nobody chases a guest from my tent, not even a feathered one.
line.sorokin_oleg.namesake_magpie.1: Hello, namesake. I borrowed my surname from your kind and never got round to giving it back.
line.sorokin_oleg.albatross_pencil.1: A black-browed albatross. In the Academgorodok's yard. This one I'll write in pencil, so I can rub it out later.
line.sorokin_oleg.nutcracker_respect.1: A nutcracker, and this close. I have no nuts on me, but a pocketful of respect.
line.kid_girl.kuzya_no_tea.1: Kuzya! Have you come to visit me? Mum says you offer guests tea. But there isn't any tea.
line.kid_girl.pigeon_hello_test.1: A pigeon. You're not a sparrow, but I'll say hello to you too. As a test.
line.kid_girl.boss_or_bird.1: Oh, someone's shouting. Is that a bird, or is it Tyoma's boss again?
line.clerk.booth_aisle.1: The owner's in the booth by the entrance, at the far end of the aisle. I'd walk you there, but I'm in the middle of a fill.
line.clerk.town_in_grey.1: Did you see the town from above, by the cable car? How many colours, roughly?
line.clerk.town_in_grey.2: I'm painting it in cells. Seven colours so far, and all of them grey.
line.clerk.night_sheet_lights.1: Did you see the town at night, from the cable car? For my night sheet I need to know how many yellow cells it takes.
line.clerk.screensaver_still.1: You're up. You sat so still I took you for a screensaver.
line.clerk.goldfinch_five_fills.1: A goldfinch. Red, white, black, yellow and beige. Five fills, and not one too many.
line.clerk.bullfinch_mixed_red.1: A bullfinch. Its breast needs a red that isn't in the standard palette. I'll mix one.
line.clerk.not_over_monitor.1: A bird in the hall? Please, just not over the monitor.
line.clerk.twelve_by_twelve.1: Don't move. You're exactly twelve by twelve cells.
line.guy_b.owner_says_odd.1: Awake? Go and see the owner in his booth. He always tells new people something, and it never makes sense.
line.guy_b.valley_way.1: Going for a walk? Good idea. I ride down every day, to work.
line.guy_b.valley_way.3: The cable car goes to the lower station, and the Academgorodok is right past it. From the station head for the sea and you'll come out on the promenade.
line.guy_b.four_places_two_by_cable.1: Four places: the beach under the cliff, the lower station, the Academgorodok, the promenade. The cable car gets you to two, the rest is on foot.
line.guy_b.never_got_swift.1: The cabins here have bird names: Starling, Chaffinch, Oriole. All the time I've been riding, I've never once got Swift.
line.guy_b.sunset_promenade_now.1: It's sunset now, go to the promenade. Cable car down, then from the station toward the sea.
line.guy_b.sunset_promenade_now.2: The beach and the rest can wait, the sunset can't. I'd go myself, but I've only just got warm.
line.guy_b.never_been_beach.1: Been all round? All the time I've been riding up and down, I've never once been down to the beach under the cliff.
line.guy_b.never_been_beach.2: Never mind. At least I know which cabin squeaks.
line.guy_b.polar_for_the_wood.1: Going north after a bird? The cable car runs to Polar Star, the end of the line. The old wood is a stone's throw from there.
line.guy_b.pigeon_comes_back.1: A pigeon in the club. That new guy fed you from his hand, didn't he? Now you all come here.
line.guy_b.robin_clean_e.1: A robin. You sing more in tune than the ventilation. Almost a clean E.
line.guy_b.phone_finally.1: Who's shrieking in the corridor? Oh, a bird. I thought somebody's phone had finally charged.
line.guy_b.no_hurry_birds.1: Stay, stay. Nobody here is in any hurry, not even the birds.
line.guy_b.sunrise_slept_warm.1: You saw the sunrise on the shore? I slept through it. Woke up warm, as if I'd been there too.
line.girl_a.lab_route.1: If you go down, look in at the Academgorodok. I work there, at Laboratory No. 2, but don't go in, it's boring.
line.girl_a.lab_route.2: From there the promenade is toward the sea. And the beach under the cliff shows from above if you step a little left off the alley, to the edge.
line.girl_a.close_but_beach.1: The cable car runs from the alley to the lower station. Everything's close from there, except the beach: that's under our own cliff.
line.girl_a.promised_sonya_sea.1: Sonya keeps asking me to take her to the promenade. I promised. Once the program works, we'll go.
line.girl_a.lights_of_academ.1: At night, head for the lights of the Academgorodok, the cable car will take you. Leave the beach till morning, it's dark under the cliff.
line.girl_a.grey_sea_still.1: It's overcast, the sea will be grey today. Go to the promenade anyway, from the Academgorodok toward the sea.
line.girl_a.grey_sea_still.2: A grey sea is still the sea. The beach under the cliff can wait for the sun.
line.girl_a.less_new_now.1: You've been all round. Funny, you don't seem quite so new now.
line.girl_a.yellow_tip_asked.1: Sonya wants to know if a waxwing's tail really has a yellow tip, as if it was dipped in paint. I told her to ask the one who saw it.
line.streamer.wave_for_chat.1: The way out? Past the machines and the owner's booth, there's an iron door.
line.streamer.wave_for_chat.2: Chat wants you to wave goodbye. Go on, it's no trouble.
line.streamer.bet_on_you.1: You're back. Chat bet you'd ride down and vanish. I bet on you.
line.streamer.sunset_just_for_me.1: You were outside, and the sun's going down. Describe it to me. Not for chat, for me.
line.streamer.soda_bets.1: Chat, he's heading for the machine. Place your bets: Baikal or Buratino?
line.streamer.punk_crest_picture.1: Chat heard you found a waxwing. Someone sent me a picture: does it really have a crest like a punk's?
line.streamer.waxwing_on_air.1: Chat, it's a waxwing! The one everybody's talking about. Don't fly off, I'll turn the camera.
line.streamer.magpie_one_mic.1: A magpie. Chat says you'll make off with my microphone. Please don't, it's the only one I've got.
line.streamer.leave_the_sound.1: Chat, hear that? That's not me, it's a bird. I'm leaving the sound in.
line.streamer.bird_more_viewers.1: A bird on camera, and chat's wide awake. Stay, I get more viewers with you.
line.streamer.wish_three_viewers.1: Chat wants shooting stars. If you see one fall, wish me at least three viewers.
line.kid_boy.went_out_once.1: Going out? It's bright out there, your eyes'll hurt. I went out once.
line.kid_boy.pines_rustle_night.1: Going out at night? It's dark and the pines are rustling. I'm not scared, I'm just on the boss.
line.guy_a.better_signal_outside.1: Going outside? If you find a spot where the signal's better, let me know.
line.owner.door_never_locked.1: The door's right past the booth. Heavy, but not locked. Nobody here ever locks it.
line.owner.door_at_sunset.1: Go on. The sun's setting, I can feel it. The door's right past the booth.
line.owner.door_at_sunset.2: Look at it for me too.
line.owner.door_sea_at_night.1: At night you can hear the sea outside. The door's right past the booth, unlocked. Follow the sound.
line.owner.whole_town_below.1: There's a whole town down there. Walk round it, no hurry. You still have time.
line.owner.news_like_draught.1: You went north after a bird. I heard. News passes this booth like a draught.
line.owner.cheerful_thunder.1: Were there fireworks? I heard them. Under the hill they sound like distant thunder, only cheerful.
line.owner.braid_crumbs.1: After the braid crumbs? Help yourself. I eat slowly, there's enough for you too.
line.owner.waxwing_from_north.1: A crest, a yellow tail. You're from the north. Your kind doesn't come here, I'd have felt it.
line.owner.back_to_the_light.1: A bird in the corridor. Fly back out, to the light. In here there are only lamps.
line.owner.on_the_threshold.1: Sitting on the threshold? A good place. Neither out there nor in here.
line.nao.pigeons_no_hurry.1: Pigeons come to people who aren't in a hurry. I checked, I stand here all day.
line.nao.cliff_from_below.1: If you go down to the beach under the cliff, see how all this looks from below. I've only ever seen it from above.
line.nao.fireworks_small_from_here.1: They say the fireworks go up from the pier. From up here they'll look small. Go down and see the big ones.
line.nao.one_lantern_faster.1: I saw the lanterns over the sea. One rose faster than the others. I decided it was yours.
line.nao.palm_pigeon_unhurried.1: Are you the pigeon that ate from the boy's palm? I saw. You took your time.
line.nao.starling_on_your_own.1: A starling. In the evening there are over a thousand of you over the sea, and now you're on your own. Not lonely?
line.nao.whole_sea_from_above.1: From up there you can probably see the whole sea. Tell me what it's like, later.
line.nao.sun_likes_this_spot.1: Sit, then. It's warm here, the sun likes this spot.
line.kid_girl.ask_owner_sun.1: Going to the owner? Ask him if the sun's out. He always knows.
line.kid_girl.stayed_up_almost.1: Mum let me stay up for the fireworks. I didn't fall asleep. Almost.
line.girl_b.wish_third_draft.1: Did you tie your wish on the bamboo? I'm still writing mine. Third draft now.
line.lange_pyotr.wish_not_fish.1: Tying a wish on the bamboo? Just don't ask for fish. Fish I can manage myself.
line.khuazhev_aslan.blini_with_cheese.1: At Maslenitsa the whole town eats pancakes. Try at least one with cheese: cheese is milk too, only patient.
